### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
Cleaning a Cast Iron Pan:

1. Start by wiping out any excess food from the pan. If there is still food sticking to the pan, you can use a plastic scraper to loosen it up.

2. Rinse the pan under hot water. Do not use soap, as it can strip the pan of its seasoning. 

3. Use a soft-bristled brush to gently scrub any remaining bits of food off of the pan. 

4. Once the pan is clean, dry it thoroughly, making sure there is no moisture left on the surface.

5. Optionally, you can use a little bit of vegetable oil to rub onto the surface of the pan, this will help keep it from rusting.

Seasoning a Cast Iron Pan:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F.

2. Apply a thin layer of vegetable oil to the entire surface of the pan, both inside and out.

3. Place the pan upside down on a baking sheet and place it in the oven.

4. Allow the pan to bake for 30-40 minutes, until it appears darker and the oil has fully absorbed.

5. Turn off the oven and let the pan cool down in the oven.

6. Once the pan has cooled down, you can use it as normal. Repeat this seasoning process as needed to keep your pan nonstick and rust-resistant.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->

### Chinese translation — EDIT HERE

<!-- ZH_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
清洁铸铁锅：

1. 首先，擦掉锅中多余的食物残渣。如果仍有食物粘在锅上，可以使用塑料刮刀将其松动。

2. 用热水冲洗锅。不要使用肥皂，因为它会去除锅的油膜。

3. 使用软毛刷轻轻刷掉锅中剩余的食物残渣。

4. 锅清洁干净后，彻底擦干，确保表面没有水分残留。

5. 可选地，可以在锅表面涂抹少量植物油，这有助于防止生锈。

给铸铁锅开锅：

1. 将烤箱预热至375°F。

2. 在锅的整个表面（内外）涂抹一层薄薄的植物油。

3. 将锅倒扣在烤盘上，放入烤箱。

4. 让锅烘烤30-40分钟，直到颜色变深且油完全被吸收。

5. 关闭烤箱，让锅在烤箱中冷却。

6. 锅冷却后，即可正常使用。根据需要重复此开锅过程，以保持锅的不粘和防锈性能。
<!-- ZH_TURN_001_END -->

If you find that using soap is the easiest and most convenient method for you, just be prepared to re-season your pan more frequently to keep it in good condition.

Certainly. The easiest way to clean your cast iron pan would be as follows:

1. While the pan is still warm, scrape out any excess food particles using a soft-bristled brush or a plastic scraper.

2. Rinse the pan under hot water. If you choose to use soap, add a small amount of soap to the water and then rinse the pan thoroughly. Make sure to remove all soap residue.

3. Dry the pan using a clean towel or by placing it over low heat on the stovetop.

4. Optionally, you can apply a small amount of vegetable oil to the pan to help prevent rust.
